hook_text: Your shop is owed R9 000. Can you name exactly who owes it? If not, you will never collect it.
clip_script: Ridgeview Hardware sells on credit in April. Five invoices: Hilltop, Ace, Hilltop again, Sunset, Ace again. Book one, the debtors journal: one line per invoice, in date order. Sales total R18 600, cost total R12 400. Book two, the debtors ledger: a page per customer. Invoices on the debit side, payments on the credit side. Hilltop owes R4 500. Ace owes R1 800. Sunset owes R2 700. Book three, the general ledger: Debtors control gets the totals. R18 600 in, R9 600 paid, R9 000 left. Now the magic check. Add the customer pages: 4 500, 1 800, 2 700. R9 000. Same answer in two places. That is how a business knows its records are right, and exactly who to phone on Monday.
visual_style: Five invoices sliding into a notebook, then splitting into three customer folders, then flowing into one big control ledger; two R9 000 totals snapping together with a green tick.
pacing: A sharp hook, three quick books, one satisfying check at the end.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and post Ridgeview's April credit sales yourself.
